newsitem.title: KENYA: Sudan group fails to free Red Cross workers.
newsitem.headline: Sudan group fails to free Red Cross workers.

text.p: A Sudanese pro-government guerrilla group has failed to release three Red Cross workers it has been holding for more than three weeks despite an agreement to do so, a Red Cross spokesman said.

An Australian nurse and two Kenyan-based pilots are held by guerrillas of the Bahr-el-Ghazal group, a breakaway from the rebel Sudan People's Liberation Army (SPLA), since their plane was grounded in south Sudan on November 1.
The group announced after talks with a representative of the International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC) on Thursday that it would free the three on Friday.
But the leader of the group, Kerubino Kwanyin Bol, later asked for a further meeting which took place on Saturday, an ICRC spokesman in Nairobi said. The three were not freed.
"They are safe and in good health -- but deeply disappointed," the spokesman told Reuters. He said efforts to secure their release would continue.

Sudan on November 7 suspended all ICRC work, saying the plane was carrying arms and troops loyal to the rebel Sudan People Liberation Army (SPLA) headed by Colonel John Garang. The ICRC denied the charge.
The plane flew from northern Kenya to Wunruk in Sudan's Bahr el-Ghazal province.
For 13 years, the SPLA has been fighting for the autonomy of the mainly Christian and animist south from Sudan's Islamist dominated north.
